answer: Craft guild apprenticeship can anchor identity: a master jade carver, a boatwright at a harbor yard or a restorer mixing umber signs for one apprentice at a time, only after witnessed bench hours and a finished piece inspected by two unrelated masters. The key binds to that signed record. Each fake head needs months of real labour and a scarce master slot, and as slots fill, an attacker must bribe ever more distant masters, who forfeit guild bonds if exposed.
